title: FAA UAP reports, batch 12 (237UAP00286 - 237UAP00310)
doc_notes: This document is a collection of FAA Skywatch incident reports regarding UAP sightings between August and October 2023.

incidents.summary: Commercial aircraft reported flashing white lights rapidly climbing and descending.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was flashing white lights rapidly climbing and descending.

incidents.summary: Aircraft reported three circling lights; primary radar target confirmed.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as three circling lights maneuvering at 40,000 feet.

incidents.summary: Multiple aircraft reported two bright lights circling at high altitude.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as two bright lights 60 miles N of BHM circling at a very high altitude.

incidents.summary: Multiple colored lights reported by aircraft and tower personnel.
incidents.quote: Aircraft reported seeing multiple colored lights and flying between BHM and HSV.

incidents.summary: Round, black and white oblong object observed by commercial flight.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was a round, black and white oblong object approximately the size of an Embraer E-145 aircraft.

incidents.summary: Multiple aircraft reported 2-4 lights with greenish hue moving in circular motion.
incidents.quote: saw 2-4 possible UAPs each having a white light with light greenish hue moving independently in a circular motion

incidents.summary: Dim white lights moving in circles and up and down patterns.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as dim white lights that would get brighter, and moved in circles and up and down patterns.

incidents.summary: Bright white light with aura reported by multiple aircraft; correlated to satellites.
incidents.quote: These reports correlate with a train of Space X satellites moving SW to NE bound.

incidents.summary: Unorganized group of white lights moving erratically.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was an unorganized group of white lights moving erratically

incidents.summary: Silver rocket-shaped object observed.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as a silver rocket approximately six feel long

incidents.summary: Moving lights reported; correlated to StarLink satellites.
incidents.quote: Report appears to correlate with StarLink satellite constellations.

incidents.summary: Multiple lights orbiting with erratic movement.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was multiple dim and bright lights orbiting with erratic movement

incidents.summary: Metallic object reported by pilot.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was described as metallic.

incidents.summary: Multiple lights orbiting, similar to landing lights.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was multiple lights orbiting. They appear to be similar to aircraft landing lights.

incidents.summary: Bright lights orbiting at high altitude.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was bright lights orbiting at a high altitude

incidents.summary: Three bright white lights blinking left to right.
incidents.quote: three bright white lights, not moving or changing altitude, blinking left to right and right to left.

incidents.summary: 4-5 lights changing direction and speed.
incidents.quote: The lights would also seem to change directions and speed.

incidents.summary: Multiple reports of potential mission failure; identified as rocket body recovery.
incidents.quote: Space OPS at ATCSCC reports the mission is a success without issue. Rocket body recovery is in process.

incidents.summary: Silver, softball-sized object.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was silver and the size of a softball and was moving W/SW bound.

incidents.summary: Unidentified object traveling at 34,000 feet.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was traveling E bound at approximately 34,000 feet.

incidents.summary: Lights traveling along the coast.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was lights traveling along the coast above their altitude.

incidents.summary: Light split into two lights flying in a crisscross pattern.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was 1 light that split into 2 lights flying in a crisscross pattern

incidents.summary: Three bright white lights, mostly stationary at high altitude.
incidents.quote: The unknown phenomenon was 3 bright white lights on a single object mostly stationary at very high altitude.
